q: How do I calculate the emissions of heating a hotel swimming pool?
title: Hotel pool heating emissions
short: Count the fuel or electricity used to heat the pool: LPG or diesel for a boiler at their default factors, or the heat pump's electricity at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh. Add the filtration pump. A pool cover cuts evaporation, which is where most of the heat is lost.
audience: Hotels, resorts and clubs with heated pools

ul: The heater: LPG, diesel or gas boiler, heat pump, or solar.
Filtration and circulation pumps, which run for long hours.
Lighting and dehumidifiers for indoor pools.

p: A sub-meter on the heat pump or the boiler's fuel log is far better than a share of the hotel bill. Without one, estimate from rated power and run hours and label it an estimate.
Boiler fuel is Scope 1 and heat pump electricity Scope 2, both inside the hotel's total. Pool heating is a useful sub-figure when comparing a boiler with a heat pump.

example.title: Worked example: boiler or heat pump for the same pool (one month, illustrative inputs)
lines: LPG boiler: 900 kg x 2.98 = 2,682 kg CO2
Heat pump: 3,600 kWh x 0.710 = 2,556 kg CO2
example.note: Fuel and electricity use are illustrative; a heat pump's actual use depends on climate and cover use.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
